common_name: Spreading Sunset Lantana (Trailing Multicolor Sunset-Toned Groundcover Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Spreading Sunset bears multicolor orange-red-yellow flower clusters on a low, trailing, groundcover-type lantana.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, and avoid overwatering, since lantana is highly drought-tolerant once established and prone to root problems in soggy soil. Spreading Sunset bears vivid multicolor flower clusters blending orange, red, and yellow tones that shift as they age, on a low, vigorously trailing plant well suited to groundcover use, spilling over walls, or filling large containers and hanging baskets. It blooms nonstop from spring through frost and draws butterflies heavily throughout the season. In the coldest parts of its hardiness range it dies to the ground in winter and returns from the roots in spring; further north it is grown as a summer annual.

common_name: Superbena Royale Verbena (Large-Flowered Vigorous Spreading Verbena Series)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained soil in full sun; Superbena Royale bears unusually large flower clusters on a vigorous, spreading, mildew-resistant verbena series.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Superbena Royale bears unusually large, showy flower clusters compared to standard Superbena selections, on a vigorous, low, spreading plant with good resistance to the powdery mildew that plagues many older verbena cultivars in humid climates. It blooms continuously from spring through frost with minimal deadheading, tolerating heat and drought well once established, and works effectively as a groundcover, container spiller, or bedding plant. Trim back lightly if growth becomes leggy in the height of summer to encourage fresh, compact regrowth.
